Connecting the output edge from none (exp 93) yields +24 to +76 points, versus a few points for replacing existing ops.
Restoring a path to the output node from none (exp 99) gives massive gains compared to swapping existing ops.
Adding a direct input-to-output path where edge 3 was none gives large gains (exps 77, 100) versus small or negative effects otherwise.
Removing a conv3x3 into the output hurts across datasets (exps 3, 53, 73), whereas removing weak ops (skip/avg_pool) in a weak cell helps.
Removing a skip_connect on edge 5 helps in the all-skip parent (+42/+39/+10) and in exp 83, unlike removing conv ops.
Upgrading a skip_connect on edge 4 to a conv yields large gains (exps 25, 35), while replacing conv3x3 with conv1x1 is neutral or negative.
Dropping edge 3 in a skip-dominated cell is much less harmful (+28 in exp 27) than in conv-heavy cells where it costs up to -16 on IN16.
Replacing a conv3x3 with avg_pool on edge 1 reduces accuracy (exps 6, 56), whereas replacing conv1x1 in a 1x1-heavy parent can help.
Replacing skip_connect on the input edge 0 with avg_pool drops accuracy on all datasets (exp 30), unlike when the parent has weaker ops.
